source: Parameters distilled and paraphrased from Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 4th ed. (Wiley, 2014). Section numbers in bci_ref cite the source. All values are preliminary-sizing rules of thumb for design plausibility checks - not a substitute for engineering analysis or the governing building code.
notes: span_range_m is the horizontal span for floor/roof/longspan systems. For wall systems span_axis is 'vertical' and span_range_m is the unsupported height range. depth_rules give depth ~= span / span_ratio. structural_material matches validate_structure's material parameter; render_material_ids link to Materialfiles material_ids so the stated construction material is reflected on the Rhino objects.

systems.name: Wood joist floor (dimension lumber)

depth_rules.note: Deflection should not exceed span/360; stiffness usually governs over strength.

elements.note: 38 mm ('2x') dimension lumber on edge; 2x6 spans to about 3.0 m, 2x12 to about 5.5 m depending on species, grade and load.
Rim joist or header closes and laterally supports joist ends; double end joists under parallel partitions.
Wood panel sheathing ties and stabilizes joists against twisting and buckling, and can act as a structural diaphragm.
Joists bear on wood/steel beams or loadbearing stud walls; lateral support required at joist ends.

construction_notes: Spacing is chosen against sheathing span rating and load magnitude.
Openings and cantilevers need doubled trimmers and headers.
Combustible light framing: fire rating comes from the finish assembly.

systems.name: Prefabricated wood I-joists and trussed joists

depth_rules.note: Rule of thumb for trussed joist depth.

elements.note: OSB or plywood web with sawn or LVL flanges; 255 mm depth spans to ~4.9 m, 305 mm to ~5.8 m, 355 mm to ~6.7 m, 405 mm to ~7.6 m.
2x4/2x6 chords with wood or tubular steel webs; depths to 1525 mm; flat wood trusses engineer up to ~27 m.
Web openings pass mechanical and electrical runs; consult manufacturer limits.

construction_notes: More dimensionally stable and longer-spanning than sawn lumber of equal depth.
Bearing conditions and allowable spans are manufacturer-specific.

systems.name: Wood plank-and-beam floor (post and beam)

typical_spacing_m.note: Beam spacing equals the span of the planks or decking.

depth_rules.note: Width 1/3 to 1/2 of depth; limit deflection to span/360.
Width 1/4 to 1/3 of depth; glulam engineered to ~24 m, LVL/PSL composites to ~27 m.

elements.note: Wood columns carry beam reactions to the foundation; larger but fewer members than joist framing.
Solid sawn, glulam, or built-up; may be exposed as finish.
Structural planking or decking spans between beams; underside may serve as ceiling.
Post-beam connections use metal straps, shear plates, split rings and through-bolts (BCI 5.49).

construction_notes: Concentrated loads and floor openings need additional framing.
Skeleton frame: wall infill is nonbearing.

systems.name: Structural steel frame floor (wide-flange beams and girders)

typical_spacing_m.note: Beam spacing = span of steel decking or precast planks; column spacing = beam or girder span.

depth_rules.note: Width 1/3 to 1/2 of depth. Use the lightest section satisfying stress and deflection.
Girders collect beam reactions to columns.
Overall composite deck depth; decking spans are short (to ~4.5 m).

elements.note: W-shape columns; orient webs parallel to the short axis of the frame.
W-shapes have superseded S-shapes; channels, tubes and composite sections also used.
Plate girders (welded plates + stiffeners) for heavy spans; castellated beams gain depth without weight.
Steel decking or precast planks span beams; composite action with concrete topping via shear studs.

construction_notes: Typical economical beam span 6-10 m; beyond that open-web steel joists become economical.
AISC framing types: moment (rigid), shear (simple) and semi-rigid connections; bolted or welded (BCI 4.17-4.18).
Noncombustible but needs applied fireproofing for rated construction.

systems.name: Open-web steel joist floor (K/LH/DLH series)

depth_rules.note: Span should NOT exceed 24 x joist depth (this is a maximum, not a target).

elements.note: Standard joists, 205-760 mm depths, spans to ~18 m.
Longspan/deep longspan, depths to 1830 mm, spans to ~44 m.
Horizontal or diagonal bridging restrains chords; required before decking.
Bearing on steel beams, joist girders, or masonry/concrete bearing walls.

construction_notes: Spacing set by decking span and joist capacity; 1.2 m common in large buildings.
Open webs pass ducts and services through the structure.

systems.name: Light-gauge (cold-formed) steel joist floor

depth_rules.note: 150 mm joists span 3.0-4.3 m; deeper sections reach ~7.9 m.

elements.note: Cold-formed C-sections; lighter and more dimensionally stable than wood, spans longer, but conducts more heat.
Rim tracks cap joist ends; web stiffeners at bearing points.

construction_notes: Noncombustible alternative to wood light framing; screwed or welded connections.
Consult manufacturer for exact sections and allowable spans.

systems.name: Cast-in-place one-way concrete slab and beams

typical_spacing_m.note: Slab spans between parallel beams or bearing walls; suited to rectangular bays (long:short > 1.5).

depth_rules.note: 100 mm minimum thickness; span/36 for roof slabs.
Beam depth in 51 mm increments; cast integrally with slab.

elements.note: Principal reinforcement one direction; temperature steel transverse.
Supporting beams frame to girders or columns.

construction_notes: Suitable for light to moderate loads over relatively short spans.
Formwork and shoring is a major cost factor (BCI 4.10).

systems.name: One-way concrete joist (ribbed/pan) slab

typical_spacing_m.note: Reusable pan forms come in 508 and 762 mm widths; rib width 125-230 mm.

depth_rules.note: 75-115 mm slab over ribs.

elements.note: Closely spaced joists cast integrally with the slab.
Transverse distribution ribs for longer spans.

construction_notes: Lighter than a solid slab of equal depth; good for light-to-moderate loads on longer one-way spans.

systems.name: Two-way flat plate / flat slab

typical_spacing_m.note: Column grid should be square or nearly square for two-way action.

depth_rules.note: Uniform 125-305 mm slab, no drops or caps; punching shear at columns governs; spans 3.6-7 m.
150-305 mm slab with drop panels (and/or column capitals) against punching shear; carries heavier loads, spans to ~9 m.
Slab depth ~= bay perimeter/180, 100 mm minimum, on edge beams between columns.

elements.note: Simplest formwork of the concrete systems; minimum structural depth.
Aligned grids; shear reinforcement or drops where loads demand.

construction_notes: Flat plates suit apartments/hotels where the slab soffit is the ceiling.
Two-way systems are more efficient on square bays (BCI 2.19).

systems.name: Two-way waffle slab

typical_spacing_m.note: Square dome forms in 485 and 762 mm sizes; rib width 125-150 mm.

depth_rules.note: 75-115 mm slab over two-way rib grid.

elements.note: Two-way ribs; solid heads at columns resist punching shear.

construction_notes: Longest cast-in-place two-way spans; the coffered soffit is often exposed.
Bay should be square or nearly square.

systems.name: Precast hollow-core plank floor

typical_spacing_m.note: Plank widths 405-2440 mm, 1220 typical; planks butt side by side.

depth_rules.note: Depths 150, 205, 255, 305 mm. Solid flat slabs (100-205 mm) span 3.6-7 m at the same ratio.

elements.note: Plant-cast, prestressed; grouted shear keys between units; optional 50 mm topping.
Bear on masonry/concrete walls, steel beams, or precast beams (rectangular, L-shaped, inverted-tee: spans 4.5-22 m, depth ~ span/15).

construction_notes: Use span ranges for preliminary sizing only; exact capacities are manufacturer span-load tables.
Prestressing gives shallower depths than site-cast equivalents (BCI 4.08-4.09).

systems.name: Precast single-tee / double-tee floor

typical_spacing_m.note: Unit widths 2440 and 3050 mm; stems 1220/1525 apart on double tees.

depth_rules.note: Depths 510-1220 mm; spans 9-36 m.
Depths 305-815 mm; spans 9-30 m; do not need temporary support against tipping.

elements.note: Prestressed stems carry the flange deck; welded plate connections between units.

construction_notes: The longest-span precast floor/roof units; common in parking and industrial structures.

systems.name: Wood platform (western) framed wall

elements.note: 2x4 (38x89) studs @405 max unsupported height 4.3 m; 2x6 (38x140) @610 max 6.1 m; story-height studs only.
Single sole plate and double top plate per story; floor joists rest on the top plates of the story below.
Wall sheathing or diagonal bracing provides lateral (racking) resistance; studs carry vertical load.
Single or double sill plate anchor-bolted to the foundation wall.

construction_notes: Each story is a platform: subflooring extends to the wall edge and serves as the work surface.
Vertical shrinkage is greater than balloon framing but equalized between floors.
Stud spacing relates to sheathing panel dimensions (1220 mm module).

systems.name: Cast-in-place concrete bearing wall

typical_spacing_m.note: Thickness rules govern rather than spacing.

depth_rules.note: Not less than 150 mm, or 1/25 of unsupported height/length between stiffening elements.
Not less than 100 mm, or 1/36 of unsupported height/length.

elements.note: Plain (unreinforced) walls need >=150 mm and height-to-thickness ratio under 22; basements/foundations >=205 mm.
Size, spacing and placement per structural engineer and code.

construction_notes: Formwork ties and finish (smooth or board-formed) decide the surface (BCI 5.07-5.09).
Walls double as shear walls for lateral stability.

systems.name: Cast-in-place concrete column grid

typical_spacing_m.note: Column spacing = beam or slab span; spacing determines imposed loads.

elements.note: A 305 mm concrete column can support roughly 185 m2 of tributary floor/roof area.
Lateral ties at regular vertical spacing restrain vertical bars.
Continuous spiral (>=10 mm dia.) with pitch <= 1/6 core diameter, clear space <= 75 mm.

construction_notes: Cast monolithically with beam/slab systems (see the concrete floor entries).

systems.name: Reinforced concrete masonry (CMU) bearing wall

typical_spacing_m.note: Vertical reinforcement >=10 mm dia. at <=1220 mm o.c. in grouted cells.

elements.note: Sum of vertical and horizontal steel at least 0.002 x gross wall section; joint reinforcement <=405 mm vertical spacing.
Reinforced bond beams at floor/roof lines and tops of walls; reinforce corners against tension.
Least dimension >=305 mm; maximum unsupported height 20 x least dimension; minimum four bars.
Openings carried by reinforced lintels or masonry arches (BCI 5.20-5.21).

construction_notes: Height-to-thickness ratio, lateral support and control-joint spacing are the critical stability factors.
Model as Concrete in validate_structure (closest available material) and say so in reporting.

systems.name: Structural steel column frame (W-shape columns)

elements.note: Allowable load depends on area and slenderness ratio L/r; a 305 mm W-column can support up to ~1115 m2 of tributary area at a ~3.7 m effective story height.
Base plates spread column loads to foundations.
Lateral stability from moment connections, diagonal bracing, or shear walls/cores (BCI 2.22-2.24).

construction_notes: Orient column webs parallel to the short axis of the structural frame.
High-rise systems graduate to braced cores, tubes and outriggers (BCI 2.24).

systems.name: Steel rigid frame (portal) roof

typical_spacing_m.note: Frame spacing = purlin span; purlins at 1.2-1.5 m = decking span.

depth_rules.note: Tapered members: shallowest at crown.
Deepest at the knee/shoulder; moment connection bolted or welded.

elements.note: Pitch 1:12 to 4:12; wall (eave) heights 2.4-9.1 m.
Channel or Z-purlins span frame to frame; eave strut at the wall line.
Rigid in-plane; must be braced perpendicular to the frames.

construction_notes: Pre-engineered metal building vocabulary; economical clear spans.

systems.name: Steel roof trusses (pitched, bowstring, flat)

typical_spacing_m.note: Purlins span the truss spacing and should land at panel points to avoid chord bending.

depth_rules.note: Depth range span/4 to span/5.
Depth range span/6 to span/8.
Parallel-chord depth range span/12 to span/20; camber or slope 1:50 minimum for drainage.

elements.note: Double angles, tees or W-shapes; gusset-plate connections.
Triangulated web carries shear as axial force.
Lateral bracing required perpendicular to the truss plane.

construction_notes: Depth allows longer spans than rolled beams; open web passes services.
Open-web steel joist roofs: joist spacing 1.2-3.0 m, span <= 24 x depth (BCI 6.12-6.13).

systems.name: Space frame roof

typical_spacing_m.note: Span 6 to 36 modules; module depth sets the two-way plate action.

elements.note: Repetitive tetrahedral/pyramidal units; behaves as a two-way plate.
Column-supported spans 9-24 m; wall/edge-supported spans 9-39 m; enlarging bearing area engages more members.

construction_notes: Supporting bay should be square or nearly square for true two-way action.

systems.name: Wood rafter roof (sloped light framing)

elements.note: 2x6 spans to ~3.0 m, 2x8 to ~4.3 m, 2x10 to ~4.9 m, 2x12 to ~6.7 m (horizontal projection, per species/grade/load).
1x6/1x8 ridge board minimum; 2x when required; structural ridge beam when ceiling joists are omitted.
Ceiling joists or rafter ties resist outward thrust; collar ties stiffen the upper third.

construction_notes: Flat roofs: minimum slope 1:50 to drains. Low-slope up to 3:12 needs membrane or roll roofing; 4:12 to 12:12 takes shingles and tiles.
Sheathing span rating must match rafter spacing.

systems.name: Wood roof trusses and trussed rafters

typical_spacing_m.note: Up to 2.4 m o.c. on decking capability; up to 6.1 m when purlins span between trusses.

elements.note: Plate-connected 2x4/2x6 members at close spacing (610 mm typical) for light spans.
Bolted/split-ring timber trusses with purlins for the longer spans (timber trusses range to ~30 m, BCI 2.20).
Load transfer at heel joints to bearing walls; lateral bracing of chords required.

construction_notes: Web members are typically 2x4 tension/compression diagonals; 2x6 where forces demand.

systems.name: Concrete shallow foundation (spread footings, walls, slab on grade)

typical_spacing_m.note: Footing plan area = column/wall load divided by allowable soil bearing pressure.

elements.note: Wall and column footings spread loads to soil; keep bearing below frost depth and on undisturbed soil.
Carries wall/floor loads to the footing; basement walls resist lateral earth pressure.
100 mm minimum, on compacted granular base with vapor retarder.
Where near-surface soil is inadequate: pile foundations (driven, to bearing strata or by friction) or drilled caissons (BCI 3.24-3.26).

construction_notes: Foundation type follows the soil profile and load magnitude; settlement uniformity matters more than absolute value.

egress_rules.source_note: Egress framework from BCI A.10-A.11 and stair rules from BCI 9.03-9.05. Numeric occupant-load factors, travel distances and separation fractions are TYPICAL IBC values (BCI defers these to the governing code) - always verify against the code in force.
egress_rules.components: A means of egress has three parts: exit access (the path to an exit), the exit itself (enclosed, fire-rated, self-closing doors swinging in the direction of travel), and exit discharge (to an exit court or public way).

exits_required_by_occupant_load.note: single exit only for small, low buildings; multi-story business generally needs two

egress_rules.signage_and_lighting: Exits identified by illuminated signs; egress paths lit by emergency lighting on power failure; exit doors swing in the direction of exit travel with panic hardware (BCI A.10-A.11).

fire_resistance.shaft_enclosure_note: Exit stair and shaft enclosures: typically 2-hr when connecting 4 or more stories, 1-hr otherwise (IBC-typical; verify). Structural steel requires applied protection - spray fireproofing, gypsum encasement, or concrete cover - to achieve a rating (BCI A.12).

reference.notes: Live loads are minimum uniformly distributed design loads by occupancy (converted from psf, 1 psf = 47.88 Pa); always verify against the governing code. Densities converted from pcf (1 pcf = 16.018 kg/m3). Source: BCI appendix A.06-A.07.
